webcpp::crypto::hybrid::basic_sealed_box

Sealed boxes: anonymous encryption to a public key.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/hybrid/sealed_box.hpp>

template<class Backend = default_backend_t<families::sealed_box>>
struct basic_sealed_box;

Description

seal draws a key pair for the message (libsodium draws it from its own generator), seals the message in a box from that key pair to the recipient’s public key, under a nonce derived from the two public keys, and writes the drawn public key, the tag and the ciphertext; the drawn secret key is wiped. Only the recipient’s key pair opens it. The recipient cannot tell who sealed it, and the sender cannot open it afterwards: a sealed box proves nothing about who wrote it.

    std::span<uint8_t const> sealed,
    std::span<uint8_t> out) noexcept;

out overlaps neither sealed nor the keys.

webcpp::crypto::random_device

The operating system’s or the browser’s generator, and nothing else.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/random_device.hpp>

class random_device;

Description

Every call reads the source: there is no cache and no generator in between. It holds no state and needs no backend. With exceptions it is a UniformRandomBitGenerator, as the standard library’s random device is; without them its interface is fill.

webcpp::crypto::secret

N secret bytes: a shared secret, a session key, a converted secret key.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/secret.hpp>

template<std::size_t N>
class secret;

Description

They are wiped by volatile stores when the object is destroyed or moved from; a copy is made only by clone.

The wipe covers the object’s own storage only: a move or a clone may leave copies of the bytes in registers or temporaries, which the library does not reach.

webcpp::crypto::error

Why an operation of webcpp::crypto failed.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/error.hpp>

enum class error : int;

Description

The values are fixed and never reused.

Members

Name Description

invalid_key_size

A key of another size than the algorithm’s key_size, or a secret key not of 32 bytes.

invalid_iv_size

A GCM IV that is empty or longer than 128 bytes.

invalid_tag_size

A tag given to open that is not of 16 bytes.

invalid_input_size

A buffer or data of a size the function does not accept: data for a block cipher that is not a whole number of blocks, or an output shorter than the function needs.

message_too_long

A message or additional data longer than the algorithm allows.

authentication_failed

The tag does not match: the message or its additional data changed, or the key differs.

invalid_state

An object moved from, or the incremental seal called out of order.

entropy_unavailable

The system’s or the browser’s generator failed.

invalid_secret_key

A secret scalar, a secret key or a tweak, that is zero or not below the group order.

invalid_public_key

A public key of the wrong size, with a prefix other than 02 or 03 (33 bytes) or 04 (65 bytes), or not a point of the curve.

invalid_signature

A signature that does not verify, or is not a valid encoding: not strict DER, or an r or an s that is zero or not below the group order.

backend_failure

A backend failed where its contract says it does not.

memory_functions_refused

OpenSSL’s memory functions could not be installed: OpenSSL has already allocated, or another party installed its own.

memory_functions_not_installed

OpenSSL’s memory functions are not webcpp::crypto’s, so a make of the OpenSSL backend refuses to run, with WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE.

weak_public_key

A public key of small order, or one that gives an all-zero shared secret.

invalid_point

An encoding that is not a canonical element of the group.

invalid_scalar

A scalar that is not reduced, or zero where zero is refused.

invalid_padding

Padding that cannot be removed, whatever the cause.

invalid_encoding

Hexadecimal, base64, PEM, or a key’s DER form that does not decode, or is not the one encoding the format allows.

invalid_ciphertext_size

A KEM or RSA ciphertext of another size than the key’s.

See Also

"Errors", in the guide.

webcpp::crypto::equal

Whether two byte sequences are equal, in a time that does not depend on their contents.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/equal.hpp>

[[nodiscard]]
bool
equal(
    std::span<uint8_t const> first_operand,
    std::span<uint8_t const> second_operand) noexcept;

Description

Every byte is read, and no branch or index depends on one: the XOR of each pair is accumulated with OR in a volatile local, read once after the loop, and reduced to one bit without a branch, as BearSSL’s tag check does. Sizes are public: spans of different sizes compare unequal without reading their contents.

Return Value

Whether they have the same size and the same bytes.

Note

The return value should not be discarded.

Parameters

first_operand

webcpp::crypto::openssl_memory_resource

The resource every allocation of OpenSSL’s in the process goes to, from any thread: declared by <webcpp/crypto/backends/openssl.hpp> under WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE and defined once by the program. It returns a resource that is never destroyed and is thread-safe whenever OpenSSL may run on two threads at once: OpenSSL frees through it after main returns.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/backends/openssl.hpp>

std::pmr::memory_resource&
openssl_memory_resource() noexcept;

Description

It must serve OpenSSL’s initialisation, which the first use of OpenSSL in the process runs, usually the first make: on an OpenSSL built with threads, which MSVC always builds, a resource that fails during OpenSSL’s base initialisation makes OpenSSL re-enter it, and that call never returns: the process aborts on macOS, deadlocks on Linux and spins on Windows. Only on an OpenSSL built without threads does it return, and every make then gives backend_failure. On Windows a thread that used OpenSSL keeps its blocks in the resource until the process ends unless it calls OPENSSL_thread_stop() before it ends.

Return Value

The program’s resource.

See Also

"OpenSSL’s allocations in your own memory resource", in the guide.

WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_THREADS

Defined when the build has threads (design D23): natively when Boost.Config defines BOOST_HAS_THREADS, on Emscripten when the program is built with -pthread (b2’s threading=multi), never on wasip2 or wasip3, and never when the program defines WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS. Only then do the heavy operations’ async_ variants run on another thread; without it, a program that calls one stops with the synchronous name to call instead.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_THREADS

Description

Natively Boost.Config defines BOOST_HAS_THREADS whatever b2’s threading says on macOS, on Windows and with libstdc++ or libc++ on Linux, so that a native build has threads unless the program defines WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS.

WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_THREADS

Defined in a build with threads, where the heavy operations’ async_ variants exist (design D23): natively unless the program defines WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS (Boost.Config’s BOOST_HAS_THREADS, which b2’s threading=single leaves defined), on Emscripten with -pthread, never on WASI.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_THREADS

WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Defined when webcpp::crypto is built without exceptions: when webcpp has none (the compiler has none, or the developer defined WEBCPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS for every webcpp library), or when the developer defines it alone.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/crypto/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Description

Every operation reports its errors as values whether or not it is defined. The random device’s operator(), whose failure could not be reported, is declared only when it is not defined.

See Also

"Exceptions", in the guide.

Appendix A: Changelog

What changed in crypto in each version of webcpp, newest first, one line per change. "Unreleased" is what the next version brings. The release notes of every version are on webcpp’s index page.

Unreleased

  • Added crypto, primitives over C backends: ciphers, curves and randomness, errors of fixed values in webcpp.crypto, every result [[nodiscard]], and WEBCPP_CRYPTO_HAS_THREADS, defined natively and with Emscripten’s -pthread unless WEBCPP_CRYPTO_NO_THREADS is.

  • Added equal, random_device, pem (PEM on libsodium), ciphers::aes128, aes192 and aes256, the AES block cipher, and ciphers::gcm, aes128_gcm and aes256_gcm: AES-GCM in place, incremental seal, failed opens zeroing data.

  • Added supports_v with its family tags, the capability table per target, default_backend_t and /webcpp/crypto//<family>-default per family and target (secp256k1’s modules among them), and refusals naming their Jamfile line.

  • Added backends::bearssl (AES-GCM alone, allocating nothing), backends::openssl via /webcpp/crypto//openssl natively and on WASI (allocating at make only, or natively in openssl_memory_resource with WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE), and backends::ctaes (block cipher alone).

  • Added curves::secp256k1: key pairs, BIP340, hedged and recoverable ECDSA, raw and hashed ECDH, strict DER, low-S, tweaks, SPKI, PKCS#8, PEM, BIP 324’s ElligatorSwift, BIP 327’s MuSig2, BIP 352’s silent payments.

  • Added curves::ed25519 and curves::x25519 on libsodium: strict verification over twelve edge cases, Ed25519ph over hash’s sha2_512 (/webcpp/crypto//crypto brings hash), the conversion, agree refusing all-zero secrets, RFC 8410’s SPKI and PKCS#8.

  • Added backends::sodium on /third_party//sodium, shared with webcpp::hash, every backend’s link-time canary and C suite, and ciphers::aead: chacha20_poly1305 (also BearSSL, OpenSSL), the original form, xchacha20_poly1305, failed seals and opens zeroing data.

  • Added ciphers::secretbox and secretbox_xchacha20poly1305, without additional data, hybrid::box, box_xchacha20poly1305 and sealed_box (failed seals and opens zeroing data), and curves::x25519::kx_keypair (crypto_kx) on libsodium, refusing peer keys of small order.

  • Added the page: chapters per namespace and use case, the memory option’s guide, generated tables, Jamfiles, messages, llms.txt, release-built sizes and throughput, X25519 timing findings (wasip2, DIT).

  • Added secret<N>, a self-wiping array that is copied only by clone, and the errors 13 to 20: memory_functions_refused, memory_functions_not_installed, weak_public_key, invalid_point, invalid_scalar, invalid_padding, invalid_encoding and invalid_ciphertext_size.
